record.paper_title: Frequently hypercyclic operators: recent advances and open problems
record.original_question: Let T be a frequently hypercyclic operator on a Banach or Hilbert space. Must T admit an invariant Borel measure of full support? If X is a Hilbert space, must T admit an ergodic measure of full support? If X is a Hilbert space, must T admit an ergodic Gaussian measure of full support? Finally, if X is a Hilbert space, must T have a unimodular eigenvalue, that is, an eigenvalue λ with |λ|=1? The source notes that the last three questions may also be asked more generally for arbitrary reflexive Banach spaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a separable infinite-dimensional Banach space and let T: X → X be a bounded linear operator. Recall that T is called frequently hypercyclic if there exists a vector x ∈ X (called a frequently hypercyclic vector) such that for every nonempty open set U ⊆ X, the set of return times N(x,U) = { n ∈ ℕ : Tⁿx ∈ U } has positive lower density, i.e. liminf_{N→∞} (1/N) · #(N(x,U) ∩ {1,…,N}) > 0.

A Borel probability measure μ on X is said to have full support if μ(U) > 0 for every nonempty open set U ⊆ X. It is T-invariant if μ(T⁻¹(A)) = μ(A) for every Borel set A, and ergodic if every T-invariant Borel set has μ-measure 0 or 1. A Gaussian measure on X is a Borel probability measure whose continuous linear images on ℝ are all (possibly degenerate) Gaussian distributions. A scalar λ ∈ ℂ is a unimodular eigenvalue of T if |λ| = 1 and there exists a nonzero vector v ∈ X (over ℂ) with Tv = λv.

Answer the following four questions:

(a) If X is an arbitrary (separable) Banach space, must every frequently hypercyclic operator T on X admit a T-invariant Borel probability measure of full support?

(b) If X is a (separable) Hilbert space, must every frequently hypercyclic operator T on X admit an ergodic Borel probability measure of full support?

(c) If X is a (separable) Hilbert space, must every frequently hypercyclic operator T on X admit an ergodic Gaussian Borel probability measure of full support?

(d) If X is a (separable) Hilbert space, must every frequently hypercyclic operator T on X have at least one unimodular eigenvalue?

Questions (b), (c), and (d) are additionally posed in the more general setting where X is an arbitrary reflexive Banach space.
artifact.category_tag: Linear dynamics and frequently hypercyclic operators
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress is known. There exists a frequently hypercyclic operator on c₀(ℤ) admitting no ergodic measure of full support, which gives a negative answer to the ergodic-full-support question on general (non-reflexive) Banach spaces; on reflexive Banach spaces one obtains a continuous ergodic probability measure giving positive mass to each nonempty open set, but full support and the Hilbert-space cases of (b), (c), (d), as well as the invariant-measure question (a), remain open as of the most recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Invariant measures for frequently hypercyclic operators
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a frequently hypercyclic operator on c0(Z) admitting no ergodic measure with full support; the question whether every frequently hypercyclic operator on a reflexive (in particular Hilbert) Banach space admits an ergodic measure of full support remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexample on c0(Z); reflexive/Hilbert case open.

status_evidence.title: Linear Dynamical Systems (Gilmore survey)
status_evidence.snippet: In the Hilbert space setting, whether every frequently hypercyclic operator admits an ergodic measure of full support, an ergodic Gaussian measure of full support, or has a unimodular eigenvalue remain open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Questions (b)-(d) remain open in Hilbert / reflexive Banach setting.
